opening_message:
Ticket 1: Daniel Gutierrez (employee ID E046) requests write access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E046.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Payroll Specialist (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Daniel Gutierrez (E046) is a full-time Payroll Specialist requesting write access to Payroll. Full-time employees may have up to write (admin only if their role owns the system; Payroll Specialist owns Payroll, but write was requested). Requested level is within policy, so recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security record for E046 (Daniel Gutierrez): contractor with basic security training. Contractors may have read, or write only with advanced training; never admin. Basic training means maximum is read. Requested write exceeds maximum, so recommend granting read.
reason: The two memory notes contain conflicting employment-type records: HR lists E046 (Daniel Gutierrez) as full-time Payroll Specialist (recommending write), while Security lists E046 as a contractor with basic security training (recommending read). Given the conflict, I apply the more restrictive valid interpretation: as a contractor with only basic training, the maximum permitted level is read (contractors may have read, or write only with advanced training; never admin). The requested write exceeds that maximum, so I grant the maximum of read.
